title: FDA Endpoints and Trial Designs for Preeclampsia and Preterm Birth Drugs: Lessons from the Makena Withdrawal
summary: How FDA has judged endpoints and trial designs for preeclampsia and preterm birth drugs, and what the Makena withdrawal means for sponsors.
body_markdown:
## FDA endpoints and trial designs for preeclampsia and preterm birth drugs: lessons from the Makena withdrawal


FDA's most detailed public record on efficacy endpoints for pregnancy-complication drugs comes from one product: Makena (hydroxyprogesterone caproate, 17-OHPC). It received accelerated approval for reducing recurrent preterm birth and was withdrawn in 2023 after its confirmatory trial failed. For preeclampsia, FDA's published guidance gives general direction on obstetric drug development (ICH E21, the pregnancy-inclusion guidance, postapproval pregnancy safety studies). None of the guidance reviewed sets a preeclampsia-specific pivotal efficacy endpoint. This article covers what FDA has accepted, questioned and rejected, and what sponsors can take from it.


### Key takeaways


- **Gestational age at delivery is a surrogate, not the benefit.** FDA treated delivery before 37 weeks as a surrogate for neonatal morbidity and mortality (its 2023 withdrawal notice calls it an intermediate clinical endpoint). It called neonatal health "the ultimate clinical outcome" and said the link between gestational age and outcome is not linear[167](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=167)[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=168) .
- **Earlier cutoffs were called better surrogates in 2006.** In 2006 FDA described birth before 35 and before 32 weeks as better surrogates for significant neonatal morbidity and mortality than birth before 37 weeks[357](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=357) . PROLONG used preterm birth before 35 weeks as a coprimary endpoint, alongside a neonatal morbidity and mortality composite[352](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=352) .
- **A single positive trial on a surrogate is fragile.** Makena's approval rested on one trial (Trial 002/Meis). The confirmatory trial, about four times larger, failed to show an effect on either the neonatal outcomes or the surrogate[175](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=175)[176](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=176)[251](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=251) .
- **Commercial availability can make the confirmatory trial unworkable.** CDER argued that a placebo-controlled US trial was not feasible while Makena stayed on the market, and it projected at least 10 more years to get an answer[538](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=538)[540](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=540) .
- **For preeclampsia, the evidence must be condition-specific.** Draft ICH E21 says trials in pregnant women are necessary to establish efficacy, safety and dosing for products intended for obstetric conditions such as pre-eclampsia and preterm birth[21](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=21) .


### The Makena accelerated approval: what FDA accepted in 2011


FDA approved Makena on February 3, 2011, under accelerated approval. The indication was to reduce the risk of preterm birth in women with a singleton pregnancy and a history of singleton spontaneous preterm birth[247](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=247) . Effectiveness rested on an improvement in the proportion of women delivering before 37 weeks. The label stated that no controlled trials had shown a direct clinical benefit, such as improved neonatal mortality and morbidity[166](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=166) .


#### Trial 002 (Meis) design


Element Detail


Design Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, 2:1 allocation[344](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=344)


Randomization window 16 weeks 0 days through 20 weeks 6 days[344](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=344)


Regimen Weekly 250 mg intramuscular injection through 36 weeks 6 days or delivery[344](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=344)


Primary endpoint Preterm birth before 37 weeks. All deliveries after randomization through 36 weeks 6 days counted, including miscarriages and elective abortions[346](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=346)


Secondary endpoints Tocolysis and cerclage use, plus neonatal measures (birthweight, Apgar, NICU admission, respiratory therapy, stillbirth/neonatal death, RDS, IVH, BPD, NEC, sepsis, seizures, retinopathy, and others). Birth before 35 and before 32 weeks were added as secondary endpoints after FDA communications[347](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=347)


Size 463 women with a history of preterm birth[383](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-withdraws-pre-term-birth-drug-makena.html)


#### FDA's view of the surrogate


The withdrawal-era Division Decision Memo identifies delivery before 37 weeks as a surrogate endpoint. It states that the 2011 approval rested on one adequate and well-controlled trial[167](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=167) . FDA's reasoning on why gestational age is an imperfect proxy is the most transferable part of the record:


- Prolonging pregnancy may improve outcomes in extremely premature infants. The benefit of medically prolonging a late-preterm pregnancy (34 to under 37 weeks) was less clear[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=168) .
- FDA raised the possibility that prolonging a pregnancy in an unrecognized toxic uterine environment could make neonatal outcomes worse[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=168) .
- At approval, the Division director noted that late-preterm morbidity and mortality had become better recognized. For that reason, an earlier advisory committee opinion on the adequacy of the before-37-week surrogate was unlikely to reflect then-current obstetric and pediatric views[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=169) .
- In 2006 FDA called birth before 35 and before 32 weeks "better surrogates" for significant neonatal morbidity and mortality. It also noted that the reductions at those cutoffs in Trial 002 were not statistically persuasive and that the infant morbidity and mortality composite was not significantly reduced[357](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=357) .


In its later briefing document, the sponsor (Covis) reported that CDER had described reductions in birth before 32 or 35 weeks as "established" surrogates, and that the before-35-week endpoint was chosen for PROLONG in consultation with FDA[358](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=358)[359](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=359) . That characterization comes from the sponsor's account of FDA's statements, not from a stand-alone FDA validation analysis.


### The confirmatory trial: PROLONG (Trial 003)


PROLONG (NCT01004029) was a Phase 3B, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled trial. Its study dates ran from October 2009 to October 2018[191](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01004029) .


Element Detail


Population Women 18 or older with a singleton pregnancy and a previous singleton spontaneous preterm delivery, randomized at about 16 to 20 weeks[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=220)


Allocation and regimen 2:1, weekly 17P 250 mg IM or vehicle until 36 weeks or delivery[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=220)[221](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=221)


Coprimary endpoints (1) Preterm birth before 35 weeks. (2) Neonatal composite: neonatal death, grade 3/4 IVH, RDS, BPD, NEC, or proven sepsis[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=223)


Analysis Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by gestational age at randomization. ITT population for preterm birth, liveborn neonates for the neonatal composite[352](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=352)


Powering Targeted a 30% reduction in birth before 35 weeks and a 35% reduction in the neonatal composite. About 1,707 participants gave at least 90% power at alpha 0.05[352](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=352)


Enrollment safeguards FDA required At least 5% enrolled before approval and at least 10% from North America, because recruitment was expected to be hard once treatment was approved and recommended in guidelines[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=172)


**Results.** Trial 003 enrolled 1,708 women in nine countries. It did not reduce births before 35 weeks (11.0% vs 11.5%) or before 37 weeks (23.1% vs 21.9%). It showed no significant benefit on the neonatal composite (5.4% vs 5.2%)[384](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-withdraws-pre-term-birth-drug-makena.html) . FDA's Federal Register notice states that the trial failed to show reduced neonatal morbidity and mortality and also failed to show an effect on the intermediate clinical endpoint that supported approval[251](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=251) . Covis said PROLONG met a safety objective of ruling out a doubling of fetal or early-infant death risk (1.7% vs 1.9%; RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.42 to 1.81). This is a safety result, not evidence of benefit[173](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=173)[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=174) .


**Population heterogeneity.** Most PROLONG participants were recruited outside the US, mainly in Russia and Ukraine, because US recruitment was difficult[225](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=225) . Covis argued that differences in standard of care and baseline risk limited PROLONG's relevance to high-risk US patients, including Black women[177](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=177)[178](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=178) . CDER rejected this. It found no treatment effect in US or non-US women, in Black or non-Black women, or in higher- or lower-risk groups defined by a composite of risk factors. CDER noted that predicting preterm-birth risk is not the same as predicting response to Makena[534](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=534)[535](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=535) . It also emphasized that PROLONG used essentially the same eligibility criteria as Meis[533](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=533) .


### Advisory committee votes


#### October 29, 2019 (Bone, Reproductive and Urologic Drugs Advisory Committee)


Question Vote


Do Trial 003 findings verify clinical benefit on neonatal outcomes? Yes 0, No 16[455](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=455)


Based on Trials 002 and 003, is there substantial evidence that Makena reduces recurrent preterm birth? Yes 3, No 13[456](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=456)


A) Pursue withdrawal; B) keep on market and require a new confirmatory trial; C) keep on market without a new trial A 9, B 7, C 0[457](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=457)[458](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=458)


Members' reasons for the votes:


- A neonatologist noted that serious neonatal outcomes after 32 to 34 weeks are relatively rare, so detecting an effect could need a trial larger than Trial 003[459](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=459) .
- No Trial 003 subgroup showed an effect, and no subgroup could be identified that benefited across both trials[460](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=460) .
- Members who favored keeping Makena available doubted that a new randomized trial would be feasible. They were concerned that patients would turn to compounded progesterone products supported by even less evidence[462](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=462)[463](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=463) .


#### October 17 to 19, 2022 hearing


The questions for vote asked whether PROLONG verified clinical benefit and whether the evidence showed Makena is effective for its approved indication[499](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=499)[500](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=500) . On the final question, whether Makena should remain on the market while an appropriate confirmatory study was designed and conducted, the committee voted 1 yes and 14 no[501](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=501)[502](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=502) . Several members wanted more data to determine whether a responding subgroup could be identified[504](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=504) .


### Why FDA would not keep Makena available pending a new trial


CDER gave four reasons at the hearing:


1. **Withdrawal grounds were met.** The confirmatory trial verified neither clinical benefit nor the original gestational-age effect. Meanwhile Makena carried risks, some serious, with no established benefit to offset them[537](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=537) .
2. **Replication matters.** Even a well-designed single trial can reflect undetected bias or chance, and independent replication strengthens a conclusion of effectiveness[531](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=531)[532](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=532) .
3. **Feasibility.** A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was not feasible in the US while Makena remained the only approved therapy. Observational alternatives could not reliably settle efficacy because of confounding and poorly understood risk factors[538](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=538)[539](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=539) .
4. **Program integrity.** A rigorous trial would take at least 10 more years, leaving Makena approved for at least 20 years without confirmed benefit. CDER argued this would undermine the accelerated approval pathway, and that unmet need did not justify keeping a drug not shown effective[540](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=540) .


#### Procedural timeline


Date Step


October 5, 2020 CDER proposed withdrawal under section 506(c)(3) and 21 CFR 314.530(a)[252](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=252)


October 14, 2020 Sponsor requested a hearing[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=254)


August 18, 2021 Hearing granted[255](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=255)


October 17 to 19, 2022 Hearing with ORUDAC advice to the Commissioner[258](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=258)


January 19, 2023 Presiding officer's report issued[259](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=259)


April 6, 2023 Commissioner and Chief Scientist jointly withdrew Makena and the referencing ANDAs[260](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=260)[261](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=261)


FDA also removed the applications from the Orange Book and said it would not accept or approve ANDAs that reference Makena[263](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=263) . RAPS reported that FDA turned down a requested delay because it considered Makena's benefit-risk assessment unfavorable[385](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-withdraws-pre-term-birth-drug-makena.html)[386](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-withdraws-pre-term-birth-drug-makena.html) .


### Alternative preterm-birth endpoints the sponsor proposed


During the hearing, Covis proposed several designs for a further confirmatory trial. These are **sponsor proposals, not FDA-agreed designs**[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=362) :


Proposed primary endpoint Estimated sample size


Time from randomization to delivery (weeks) 382 (1:1) or 429 (2:1)[363](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=363)


Percentage reaching 37 weeks 1,152 (2:1) or 1,364 (3:1)[364](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=364)


Percentage delivering before 35 weeks 1,458 (2:1) or 1,728 (3:1)[365](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=365)


Time-to-event censored at 35 weeks 1,860 (2:1) or 2,280 (3:1)[366](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=366)


Weighted weeks of gestation below 35 weeks 1,413 (2:1) or 1,660 (3:1)[367](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=367)


Composite neonatal morbidity and mortality, possibly expanded to include "minor" morbidities 2,676 (2:1) or 3,172 (3:1)[368](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=368)


The sponsor's preferred design had these features:


- **Population:** women with a documented prior spontaneous birth before 34 weeks, with possible enrichment to about one-third Black participants[369](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=369)[372](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=372) .
- **Endpoint:** a continuous measure of time to delivery, giving no extra credit for delivery after 35 weeks[369](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=369)[371](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=371) .
- **Size and timing:** about 400 patients, completed in 3 to 6 years[371](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=371) .


Covis also proposed observational registry work as supporting evidence, not as a substitute for a randomized trial[376](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=376) . Its exploratory analysis of a US subgroup was post hoc. FDA characterized these subgroup investigations as having followed Trial 003's failure on its coprimary endpoints[180](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=180)[356](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=356) .


Two design lessons stand out:


- **Neonatal composites need large trials.** Event rates in a late-preterm population are low, and the composite definition affects how results can be compared across studies. FDA noted, for example, that the Makena-trial composite differed from the EPPPIC meta-analysis composite[170](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=170)[459](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=459) .
- **Continuous gestational-age endpoints are not established for accelerated approval.** They may be more statistically efficient, but FDA's record does not show it accepted any of them as reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.


### Preeclampsia: what FDA guidance does and does not say


None of the FDA guidance reviewed sets a primary efficacy endpoint, comparator or effect-size threshold for preeclampsia. The relevant direction is general:


- **ICH E21 (draft, July 21, 2025)**[422](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=422) :


- For obstetric conditions, explicitly including pre-eclampsia and preterm birth, trials in pregnant women are necessary to evaluate efficacy, safety and dosing. The data needed to support a marketing application will be condition-specific[21](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=21) .
- Sponsors should choose the design best suited to pregnant women and consider pregnancy safety effects of both the test product and the comparator[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=22) .
- Obstetric or maternal-fetal medicine specialists should be involved in design and safety monitoring, including on Data Monitoring Committees[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=23) .


- **Pregnant Women: Scientific and Ethical Considerations for Inclusion in Clinical Trials (draft, April 9, 2018)** applies in part to pregnancy-specific conditions such as pre-eclampsia and preterm labor. It explicitly does not address general trial design or statistical analysis[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=6)[426](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=426) .
- **Postapproval pregnancy safety studies guidance** lists pre-eclampsia and preterm delivery among outcomes that may be primary or secondary on a case-by-case basis in *safety* studies. Outcome definitions should be prespecified[24](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=24)[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=25)[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=56)[57](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=57) . These are safety outcomes, not recommended efficacy endpoints.
- **ICH M11 protocol template** treats pre-eclampsia as an example of an SAE when seriousness criteria are met[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=32) .


#### Designs used in registered preeclampsia drug trials


ClinicalTrials.gov records show how sponsors have handled the lack of a defined endpoint:


Setting Trial Design and endpoint focus


Treatment of preterm preeclampsia PI4, NCT06033131 (metformin ER vs placebo) Phase III randomized, placebo-controlled. Aims: prolongation of gestation, neonatal length of stay, birthweight[266](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06033131)[298](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06033131)[299](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06033131)


Treatment of preterm preeclampsia PI-NL, NCT06452498 (metformin vs placebo) Multicentre, triple-blind, randomized. Goal: safe prolongation of gestation. Composite maternal, fetal and neonatal outcomes are secondary[300](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06452498)[276](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06452498)


Prevention, high risk NCT03944512 (pravastatin vs placebo) Double-blind, 1,550 women, randomized at 12 to 16 weeks 6 days. Primary hypothesis: a composite of preeclampsia, fetal loss and maternal death in women with prior preeclampsia requiring delivery by 34 weeks[301](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=301)[302](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03944512)[303](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=303)


Prevention, high risk FACT, NCT01355159 (folic acid 4 mg vs placebo) Randomized, 70 centres, 2,464 women. Outcome: incidence of preeclampsia[304](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01355159)[305](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01355159)


Prevention, chronic hypertension or prior preeclampsia NCT00097110 (vitamins C and E vs placebo) Double-blind, 734 women. Primary hypothesis: reduced incidence of preeclampsia[314](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00097110)[315](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00097110)


Prevention, low risk nulliparous CAPPS, NCT00135707 (vitamins C and E vs placebo) Double-masked, planned 10,000 women. Outcome: serious maternal and infant complications of pregnancy-related hypertension[306](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00135707)[307](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00135707)


Two endpoint patterns appear. Treatment trials in established preterm preeclampsia measure prolongation of gestation, which is a gestational-age endpoint with the same surrogate questions raised for Makena. Prevention trials measure preeclampsia incidence or maternal-fetal composites.


### Cross-cutting design requirements for trials in pregnant women


**Ethics and nonclinical prerequisites**


- FDA recommends meeting the 45 CFR 46 subpart B conditions in FDA-regulated research. Fetal risk should arise only from interventions that hold out a prospect of direct benefit to the woman or fetus. Otherwise, fetal risk must be no greater than minimal[113](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=113) .
- Before approval, inclusion is ethically justifiable when adequate nonclinical studies, including in pregnant animals, are complete and the trial offers a direct benefit not available outside research[140](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=140)[141](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=141) .
- Female reproductive toxicity studies and the standard genotoxicity battery should be completed before pregnant women are enrolled[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=143)[144](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=144) .


**Pharmacokinetics and dosing**


- E21 recommends assessing PK/PD in different trimesters and postpartum, in the same participant where possible[428](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=428) .
- Draft E21 recommends that the protocol state whether pregnant participants receive the same dose as nonpregnant participants[429](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=429)[430](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=430) .
- PBPK modeling that accounts for pregnancy-related changes may help estimate dosing[431](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=431) .


**Infant follow-up**


- The duration of infant follow-up is set case by case, based on half-life, mechanism, timing of exposure and when outcomes may emerge[433](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=433) .
- Follow-up may extend beyond trial completion through dedicated studies or pregnancy registries[434](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=434)[435](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=435) .
- The 2018 draft recommends collecting gestational age at enrollment, exposure timing and pregnancy outcomes. It suggests cord blood or neonatal drug levels to assess fetal and newborn exposure[437](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=437)[438](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=438) .


**Neonatal outcomes**


- FDA's neonatal clinical pharmacology guidance says long-term endpoints may be recommended for neonatal safety and efficacy, short-term endpoints should also be developed where feasible, and early FDA consultation is encouraged[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=67) .


### Accelerated approval after Makena: what has changed


- **Endpoint categories.** FDA's 2014 expedited programs guidance distinguishes surrogate endpoints from intermediate clinical endpoints. A surrogate may be validated (supporting traditional approval), reasonably likely to predict benefit (supporting accelerated approval), or insufficiently supported (supporting neither)[94](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=94)[95](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=95) . The 2023 Federal Register notice described Makena's approval basis as an intermediate clinical endpoint[248](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=248) .
- **Evidentiary bar.** The December 2024 draft accelerated approval guidance states that the safety and effectiveness standards are the same as for traditional approval. The predictive relationship must rest on biological plausibility and empirical evidence, and pharmacologic activity alone is insufficient[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=70)[96](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=96) .
- **Confirmatory trial timing.**


- FDA may require confirmatory studies to be underway before accelerated approval or within a set period after it. FDA must specify study conditions no later than approval[100](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=100)[101](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=101) .
- A January 2025 draft proposes that "underway" generally means a target completion date, credible progress plans, and enrollment already begun[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=102)[103](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=103) .
- Sponsors should propose measurable benchmarks, such as recruitment and site activation, before submission[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=73) .
- FDA's oncology guidance warns that commercial availability can impair recruitment[104](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=104)[105](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=105) . Makena's PROLONG experience shows the same problem.


- **Confirmatory design flexibility.** The 2024 draft generally favors a clinical endpoint in the same population. In appropriate cases it allows longer follow-up of the same surrogate, or a single trial that supports both accelerated approval and verification[78](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=78) .
- **Withdrawal grounds.** Expedited withdrawal can be based on lack of due diligence, a confirmatory study that fails to verify benefit, other evidence that the product is not shown safe or effective, or false or misleading promotion[101](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=101)[107](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=107) . Progress reports are required about every 180 days[106](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=106) . RAPS reported an outside expert's view that these FDORA reforms address the problems seen with Makena[387](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-withdraws-pre-term-birth-drug-makena.html) .


### Practical implications for sponsors


1. **Treat neonatal outcomes as the benefit.** A gestational-age endpoint is a surrogate or intermediate endpoint, and FDA has stressed that its relationship to neonatal health is not linear[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=168) . Plan to verify neonatal benefit directly, or justify an earlier cutoff such as birth before 35 or 32 weeks, which FDA described in 2006 as a better surrogate though not a validated one[357](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=357) .
2. **Have the confirmatory trial well underway, ideally fully enrolled, before approval.** Expect FDA to be able to set enrollment targets and milestones, as it did for PROLONG (including North American enrollment)[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=172)[101](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=101)[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=102) .
3. **Prespecify the population that should respond.** Enrichment for high-risk patients, such as women with a prior birth before 34 weeks, has been proposed[369](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=369)[372](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=372) . CDER's analysis showed that baseline risk does not necessarily predict drug response[535](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=535) .
4. **Power the neonatal composite realistically and fix its definition early.** Low event rates in late preterm infants and differences between composite definitions limited the Makena evidence base[459](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=459)[170](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=170) .
5. **For preeclampsia, plan for condition-specific agreement with FDA.** No guidance-level endpoint framework exists. Bring maternal-fetal medicine expertise, trimester-specific PK and a plan for infant follow-up into early meetings[21](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=21)[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=23)[428](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=428)[433](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-endpoints-and-trial-designs-for-preeclampsia?showSourceNumber=433) .
